title: Maximum Good Subtree Score
summary: Given an undirected tree rooted at node 0 with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, where each node has an integer value and a parent is specified, you need to find the maximum possible sum of values for a good subset of nodes within each subtree, including the node itself and all its descendants.
statement: Given an undirected tree rooted at node 0 with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, where each node has an integer value and a parent is specified, you need to find the maximum possible sum of values for a good subset of nodes within each subtree, including the node itself and all its descendants. A subset is considered good if every digit from 0 to 9 appears at most once in the decimal representation of the values of the selected nodes. Sum these maximum possible sums and return the result modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: The rooted tree has up to 500 nodes and par[0] is -1.
Across selected node values, every decimal digit zero through nine may appear at most once.
For each subtree find its maximum good-subset sum, then return the sum of those maxima modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: The goodness constraint is fully represented by a ten-bit mask of digits already used.
Compute a mask-sum knapsack bottom-up for every subtree, rejecting node values with repeated internal digits.
Initialize empty and optional-node states; merge each child using only disjoint masks; add the table maximum to the answer.
Every good subset splits uniquely into independent child-subtree subsets plus an optional root, and disjoint-mask merging enforces exactly the global digit condition.
editorial: Every good subset splits uniquely into independent child-subtree subsets plus an optional root, and disjoint-mask merging enforces exactly the global digit condition.
